recommendations.text: There are deficiencies in the execution of local movement in the protected zones. The Portuguese authorities are requested to make the execution coherent with the provisions laid down in Council Directive 77/93/EEC. Deficiencies were found on the Azores. As the visits were limited to the Azores and the region Ribatejo e Oeste, it is recommended that, when a similar situation occurs in other regions in Portugal, the recommendations should also apply to those regions.

Regarding the return of soil to the production fields of sugar beets, it is recommended that the DSPPA takes measures to ensure that the soil is returned to the field from which it originates. This limits the risk of Rhizomania spreading in the event of late discovery.
DGPC is urged to carry out an investigation, if necessary in co-operation with the DRA's, to the extend local movement is applied in Portugal (see conclusion 6.4). 5

audits.title: Import of Canadian seed potatoes under derogation

recommendations.text: The system laid down in the Decision can not function, as long as the separation of lots already from the beginning onwards is not ensured. Numbered labels and colour codes facilitate significantly the identification of bags and therefore the work of the inspectors, but the lots must in any event be kept separately already by the exporting country.

In the present case of imports to Portugal it is highly recommended to try to find out the real number of bags imported and also the number of bags and the respective lots sold to the agricultural co-operatives.

As a third vessel is still expected for the next weeks, it should be taken into account, to carry out an inspection at the arrival of it. If it shown, that the lots are not loaded separately, a refusal of the consignment is recommended. Only such a stringent measure taken already at the beginning of the chain of trade can force the exporter to follow the prescriptions precisely.

It is obvious, that the loading and shipment in Canada are the bottlenecks of the whole procedure. Therefore, future inspections should be carried out with priority on these aspects. With a second priority, the unloading procedure in the relevant Member State should be another key point for inspections.
A suggested solution could be the shipment of each separated lot in a separate container. 3
Legislation introducing a complete feed ban on MMBM for all livestock species should be implemented.16

The complete feed ban may be reconsidered in view of the implementation of the following conditions: · An effort to trace all the amounts of incompletely treated MMBM including feedstuff in which such MMBM is present or may be present by cross contamination should be made. This material should not be used in the feed chain. The Portuguese authorities should be required therefore to provide figures on the stocks still existing of incompletely processed MMBM, feedstuff batches in which such MMBM may be present, and MMBM and feed containing MMBM produced with SRMs and the measures taken to avoid their use in the feed chain.17 · Measures to dispose of dead ruminants and SRMs should be implemented. · Active collaboration from practitioners is required to increase the feed ban awareness. Any breach of the feedban should be actively followed-up by the Veterinary authorities and effective dissuasive measures should be put in place. · The central veterinary authorities should redirect the BSE surveillance in view of the performances of the local veterinary authorities. The epidemiological information collected at field level on BSE cases should include more detailed information on possible feed-ban breaches and on the origin of all the feedstuff introduced in the farm considering the incubation period of the disease. · The frequency of the official controls should be related to the availability of auditable written procedures in the industry. · Microscopic tests in feedstuff samples should be carried out to ensure the implementation of the MMBM ban. 16 The Portuguese authorities in their comments on the draft provided on 25.9.98, declared that such a measure will be appropriate and will have practical effects if applied to all Member States. 17 According to the Portuguese authorities there are no stocks of MMBM to be reprocessed and legislation to prohibit the use of SRMs in the feed chain has been approved. However in the opinion of the ScVC of 26-27 March 1998, as updated by the Steering Committee of 24-26 September 1998, on saftey of MMBM, it is reported that: "Cannot be excluded that under the worst conditions traces of infectivity could remain (after processing) and in order to minimize a possible remaining risk of infectivity SRMs shall be excluded from the feed chain". As a matter of fact this risk has been reduced only after the implementation of the legal measure announced by the Portuguese authorities and therefore it is not excluded residual exposure by cross contamination or cross feeding. 15
Details on the relations between the positive case discovered by histology and the clinical case should be provided to the Commission. 18

A specific enquiry is required to clarify if the animal fat used in one of the plants visited was produced in accordance with Community legislation and to ensure that fat produced from low risk waste is not used for human consumption. 19
A programme for full implementation of Directive 90/667/EEC and Commission Decision 96/449/EC should be provided to the Commission.20
Commission Decision 97/735/EC should be implemented without further delay.

A follow-up mission should be carried out to further verify the control measures to eradicate BSE. 18 According to the Portuguese authorities a report is going to be prepared on this point. 19 The Portuguese authorities in their comments on the draft provided on 25.9.98 declared that the Minister of Agriculture launched an inquiry on this item on 8 September 1998. 20 The Portuguese authorities with their comments on the draft report of 25.9.98 provided an activity program on this point from which inspections to rendering plant processing animal waste other than mammalian has been launched. 16
The Portuguese authorities should continue to accumulate additional data on the immuno-blotting test and present it to the Commission.

The Portuguese authorities should continue the eradication programme in order to eradicate the disease from the remaining areas of Portugal. 8.2. To the European Commission: 8.2.1 The Scientific Veterinary Committee should examine all relevant data in relation to the immuno-blotting test for the diagnosis of C.B.P.P. with a view to establishing harmonised protocols for the inclusion of this test in E.U. law. 12 8.2.2 The eradication programme should be financed for 1999 in order to eradicate the disease from the remaining areas of Portugal. 13
In view of the control measures in place, the possibility of re- introduction of vaccination of young animals in areas where the disease situation is explosive should be considered.
Measures should be taken to enforce national legislation and Community legislation (Dir. 92/102/EEC) on animal identification in small ruminants without undue delay.
Animal movement control should be improved. Introduction of individual ear-tag numbers in the PISA would be an important aid in the control of animals introduced on farms.

As a matter of urgency, corrective action should be taken to address the deficiencies under chapter 6 in order to respect both the conditions laid down in the approved BM eradication programme and Community legislation.

The pasteurisation process of sheep and goat milk should be closely monitored. A report indicating the action proposed, and the time span needed to implement this action, should be submitted to the Commission within 30 working days upon receipt of this report. 7.2. To the Commission services: 7.2.1. Recommendations will be made in a general report when all the inspection missions on the BM eradication programme have been completed. 21

audits.title: Fresh meat establishments and trade in fresh meat

recommendations.text: Recommendations to the competent authority of Bulgaria It is recommended that: · the pace of identification of livestock be accelerated; · draft legislation including animal welfare be implemented as soon as possible; 8 · that the veterinary services ensure adequate record keeping in the Central Veterinary Laboratory for Exotic Diseases; · the veterinary services ensure, before proposing milk plants producing sheep cheese for approval of import into the European Union, that structural problems be solved, a HACCP programme be implemented and that the raw material be grade A sheep milk only; · the veterinary services either suspend import of meat into the European Union from one slaughterhouse, where deficiencies have been identified, until it is brought up to standard, or delist it. A report on the actions taken should be submitted to the services of the European Commission within one month.

Recommendations to the services of the European Commission It is recommended: · to lift the restrictions on the imports of bovine, ovine and caprine animals into the European Union from certain banned regions in Bulgaria, except from the 20 km border zone with Turkey, provided that the animals are subjected to a quarantine period of 15 days under official supervision prior to the import into the European Union; · to lift the restrictions on the imports of bovine and sheep meat into the European Union from certain banned regions in Bulgaria, except from the 20 km border zone with Turkey. 9

audits.title: Animal welfare on-farm and during transport

recommendations.text: The competent authority submitted comments on the draft report which were taken into consideration prior to the preparation of the final report.

In their written comments of 18th February 2000 the Portuguese authorities wish to point out that they consider the legal amendments made, the regulations issued and the training courses given represent progress in the field of the protection of animals during transport. 18

Immediate extension of surveys outside the current infested zone to high risk pine areas (those in proximity to wood processing facilities) and to wood processing facilities. Sampling at the processing yards should include the wood itself plus chip/bark piles as well as trace- back of sources of wood supplied to the mills. Surveys in the forests should take account of the likelihood that PWN infestation of living trees may not lead to wilt symptoms taking account of the lower average temperatures in more northerly locations. Samples should include recently dead trees, those showing wilt symptoms and, to a lesser extent, live trees.
Systematic surveys of all remaining pine areas using the methods mentioned above.

For the year 2000 flight season, flight traps for the presence of Monochamus spp. should be established in forest locations and at wood processing facilities in both the PWN-infested and currently non-infested areas. The traps should be based on a more open design, such as funnel traps or cross-vane traps, and should include monoterpene attractants (further details about traps and the most suitable attractants should be assessed from the literature). Vectors should be sampled for the presence of PWN.
The quarantine regime imposed on the infested area should be published officially as soon as possible.

Reports for the services of the Commission should be prepared: - Final action plan for activities to be carried out in the infested area during the winter period (by 1 November 1999). - Action plans for surveys of high risk pine areas and for national surveys (by 31 December 1999). 5 The Portuguese authorities mentioned, that the trap logs, which are deployed and which will be investigated, will provide important information on the presence of vectors. 17 - Detailed analysis of the results of the present survey, including PWN incidence, beetle infestation in trees and trap logs, etc. (by 31 December 1999). - Results of winter actions (by 1 May 2000). - Assessment of potential trade pathways within Portugal and to other countries, especially EU Member States, concentrating on recent historical records of movements of wood products and packaging and their destinations (covering at least the last three years). Further data sources than those available at present to the DGF and DGPC must be taken into account (by 31 December 1999). - Results of all surveys and activities carried out in the next year (by 31 December 2000). 7.2. Recommendations to the Commission Services (1) PWN should be moved from Annex II.A.I. to Annex II.B., declaring all other Member States except Portugal as a protected zone. As information about possible spread of PWN within Portugal is still very limited, no provision be made for regionalisation of Portugal. (2) In Annex IV.B the same special heat treatment and equivalent requirements already in place for imports from Third countries where PWN is known to occur (as laid down in Council Directive 77/93/EEC, Annex IV.A.I Nr.1.1-1.5), should be established for the introduction and movement of wood of conifers into this protected zone. (3) Annex V.A.II should also be adapted, in order to ensure that an EEC plant passport accompanies exports of wood of conifers from Portugal to other Member States. (4) A follow-up inspection should be carried out in the 1st semester 2000 in order to make another assessment of further activities carried out by Portugal. 18
The Program for the inspection on the farms and in particular the selection of the farms on the basis of the criteria foreseen by the Commission Regulation 2630/97 has not been drafted;
It was not completely clear whether the yearly amount of premium per farm was taken into account as one of the criteria to perform a well balanced selection of farms to be visited;

A number of comments should be made on the results of these three inspections: · no comments were provided on the completeness and regularity of the passport, even though the passports, as already in previous missions (XXIV/1044/99 and XXIV1061/99), show delay between the date of birth and the date of issue; · no comments were provided on the absence , in the farm register, of the date of entry of animals; in particular, this was observed for the cattle already present in the farm when a new Herd Register was built up; · A single form of declaration of movement of cattle (issued in October) was used to declare 2 cattle sold in June, 1 cattle dead in May, 1 cattle sold in July and 2 cattle sold in October; · Neither actions nor deadlines to correct the situation, which were requested from the farmer, were registered. · The administrative sanctions for the problems identified in the farms will be applicable in a near future, to avoid a difficult approach in this first phase of the control system. · The information already present in the SNIRB System is the basis to carry out specific inspections: in fact, the procedure for the animal identification inspection foresees that a printout of the inventory for the specific farm must be provided to the inspectors to verify if the information in the SNIRB has to be updated. However, in the farm visited, inspection did not result in the updating of the database. II.3.2 The SNIRB System II.3.2.1 Architecture of the system The system consists of a central database (Oracle8 & Application Server) and 100 local client PCs. Each client has a Web browser installed and the client application is down-loaded from the server as an applet. The Application Server handles requests made by the clients allowing them direct access to the database. II.3.2.2 Structure of the database Detailed documentation on the data model and table descriptions was provided to the mission team. Ear-tags, animals, holdings, farms, hauliers and movements represent distinct entities in the database. However, the database does not currently contain any flags related to movement restrictions or irregularities detected during official controls. The Graphical User Interface is relatively user friendly although it does not yet provide 7 DG(SANCO)/1227/1999/MR Final all the functionality needed for tracing purposes. Currently the options available for the end-user are limited to a set of relatively simple queries i.e. movements of a given animal, animals on a given holding, etc. On the other hand, the user interface enables users also to run some resource-intensive queries (for example: number of notified births for each municipality), which block the system from other users for a while, reducing the availability of the system. Queries that are not included in the user interface can be constructed at the central level on an ad-hoc basis. II.3.2.3 Setting up of the database The database was set up during May and June 1999. Each keeper of bovine animals had to present the passports and herd-registers in his/her possession to one of the 500 collection points set up by agricultural federations and complete a written notification listing all the animals in the holding. This information was then forwarded to INGA, which brought the data into the system. The initial notification resulted in 1 117 427 bovines (in approx. 87 000 holdings) being registered on 24.6.1999. The notification of births, movements and deaths became obligatory only after this initial period of pre- notifications. The database is able to register the dam; however, this depends on whether the farmers provided this information in due time. According to the PA declaration, the percentage of not registered dams is large but unknown. II.3.2.4 Updating of the database The flow of data during updates is identical to the one described above. This means, that a delay of a few days between the notification and the actual updating of the database can not be avoided. In addition to the notifications made by keepers at the collection points, 100 local PCs connected to the system are capable of modifying and updating the database. According to Portuguese Authorities all 25 abbattoirs and 7 regional services are already connected to the system and have access to the data. The keepers do not currently have access to the database but the Portuguese Authorities are planning to implement a system of sending regular feed-back to each keeper in order to enable them to identify and fix incorrect data. II.3.2.5 Validation of input Currently validation of input data is restricted to routine type-checking and in certain cases, checking that the data fits within given boundaries. Validation rules applied during input are currently being identified and are to be implemented in near future. In the meantime, invalid or contradictory data may be entered into the database and was explained to be subject to review with necessary actions at a later stage. At the time of the mission the method of review and/or actions was not clearly defined. Existing data (i.e. PISA and SINGA) or data collected during on-farm visits is not systematically exploited to validate the contents of the SNIRB database. Moreover, actions to assure the logical integrity of the database are not foreseen at the moment. However, a certain degree of logical integrity is achieved by using the built in mechanisms in Oracle8 for maintaining referential integrity. II.4 The BSE surveillance and eradication 8 DG(SANCO)/1227/1999/MR Final II.4.1 The tracing operations As regards the tracing operations: during the meeting with the Regional Veterinary Services it was clarified that a BSE case file is considered as "closed" when all the available information are gathered and all the efforts have been done to trace the animals. On this basis, the PA have calculated that between 20 and 30% of the cases (1998/1999) can be considered closed; the others need further investigations. However, this does not mean that all the animals involved in a BSE case have be traced. According to the declaration of the Portuguese authorities, the tracing operations allowed to find 10% of animals to be traced because at risk, so far. II.4.2 The controls carried out in the veterinary laboratories Two veterinary laboratories are involved in the BSE controls: the National Veterinary Laboratory in Lisbon (LNIV) and the one located in Porto. In the meeting with the staff from the two labs, it was possible to clarify that: · The process of accreditation of the Labs has been speeded up and it should be completed in the middle 2000. The Responsible for the Quality Assurance has already presented the request for the official visit of the Agency authorised for the assessment. Most of the first steps (declaration of the quality policy, definition of the specific responsibilities, drafting of the Standard Operational Procedures) have already been done; · The ring test -already planned as the last step in a 3 year EU financed research project - will certainly result in the harmonisation of the whole set of techniques; · The standard procedures foreseen in the OIE standard (Chapter 3.2.13) are properly applied. LNIV is normally carrying out 6 samples (behind obex, obex, medulla, and midbrain) and it means one location more than in the above mentioned standard. The examinations are carried out in parallel even though the feeling of the mission team is that the result of the midbrain examination is not properly taken into consideration; · The data concerning the isolation of Listeria in the positive and negative BSE cases is worrying: in 30% of the BSE positive cases and in 54% of the BSE negative cases LNIV Listeria is isolated as well. The analytical method for Listeria is the so-called "Rapid test" and an histopathological confirmation is not always carried out; II.4.3 The enforcement of the Surveillance Plan As regards the specific recommendations on the enforcement of the Surveillance Plan (see Report XXIV/1061/99: the incorporation of the fallen stock and the emergency slaughtering in the category of cattle to be sampled), only recently the PA has sent a specific instruction to the DRAs. As a consequence, only in the following missions will it be possible to evaluate the results of this improvement. In particular, according to the declaration of the PA and considering the relatively low number of slaughterhouses, a centralisation of the collection of samples for the emergency slaughtering will be possible, if necessary. As regards the fallen stock, it must be remembered that the declaration of death is now compulsory, because of the recently adopted rules on the animal identification system. II.4.4 The burial of fallen stock 9 DG(SANCO)/1227/1999/MR Final As regards the burial of the fallen stock, the situation is already described in Report XXIV/1061/99: as agreed with the PA, there is an obvious need to improve the juridical framework and, subsequently, specific instructions will be drafted. For the moment, the burial is practically used as one of the ways to eliminate fallen stock, also for the BSE positive cases, as already discussed with the Regional Veterinary Services in Entre Douro e Minho during the mission carried out in June 1999 (see Report XXIV/1061/99). In the meeting with the competent authority of Region of Beira Litoral the burial was declared to have been the method to dispose of 17 BSE positive cases out of 20 (only 3 were slaughtered in one of the dedicated plants). II.4.5 The BSE training The BSE specific training was always addressed by the staff as one of the needs: in one of the plant visited, despite the number of staff (6 veterinarians, 5 auxiliaries and 2 Specific technicians for the SRM controls) the last training course (December 1998) was attended only by the 2 technicians dedicated to the SRM controls. II.4.6 The vigilance in the slaughterhouses The vigilance in the slaughterhouses depends very much on the capability of the staff, and this is because of the lack of instructions and also the lack of training: in one of the 2 plants the ante mortem inspection was not appropriate: · because of the lack of facilities on the plant; · because, according to the declaration of the staff, in case of any health problem in one of the animal the only decision to be taken is to slaughter the animal at the end of the slaughtering day. The weakness of the controls in the ante mortem inspection was observed in different areas: in the specific BSE area (no BSE suspect animals in the emergency slaughtering operations, even though the clinical symptoms registered by the staff could not exclude BSE) and also in the animal identification area (where a not properly identified animal can have access for the human consumption, after the farmer have paid a sanction that could result in the commercial value of the animal). A different situation was observed in the second slaughterhouse, approved on the basis of the foreseen derogation of the ''vertical rules'' on red meat production. II.5 The SRM controls in place II.5.1 The controls in place in the plants There was no change in the rules regarding the removal of SRM in the slaughterhouse and the storage of the meat and bone meal/tallow to be destroyed. The PA are still defining the SRM in a broader way than Commission Decision 98/272/EC (see Report XXIV/1044/99) and a further plant, as declared in the monthly Report sent by PA to Commission, had to be approved to support the production of MBM from SRM. According to the declaration of the PA, an incineration plant in a Member state could be interested in destroying the MBM in a near future, subject to a preliminary inspection visit as laid down in the Commission Decision 98/653/EC, as amended by Commission decision 1999/713/EC. II.5.2 The specific situations 1. As regards the operations in the slaughterhouses: 10 DG(SANCO)/1227/1999/MR Final · The removal of the tonsils is carried out as already observed in a previous mission (XXIV/1044/99): the decision to keep the tonsils attached to the tongue results in a further intervention on the tongue (to guarantee that the tonsils, considered SRM, are completely removed and eliminated) · The SRM staining is carried out by a spray system that results in a better colouring; however, after an inspection of the lorry dedicated to the delivery of SRM to the processing plant the mission team noted that the staining was not completely effective; · The truck dedicated to the delivering of SRM was neither leak-proof nor labelled; · In the SRM loading area SRM and Low Risk Material were placed together waiting to be loaded; · Often the processing plant does not send back to the slaughterhouse the copy of the accompanying document (to certify that the consignment has arrived at the plant of destination). 2. As regards the operations in the processing plant: · In case of consignments from different plants, there often are discrepancies or missing information on the accompanying documents as regards the weight and the number of seals on the specific parts of the consignments; · The supervision of the competent authority is well organised and the reconciliation of the incoming and outgoing material is properly carried out; · The documents accompanying the SRM consignments can be not only be the foreseen certification (Guia de transporte) but also a commercial invoice; · No registration of the sealing of the truck (the seals are not numbered) was carried out. III. CONCLUSIONS III.1 Developments on the legislation and administrative instructions Some improvements were made to adapt the legislation and the specific instructions to the recommendations of the previous mission (see report XXIV/1061/99). Above all, the adoption of an amendment of the Decree Law 28/84 represents certainly an important instrument to control the efficacy of the export ban: in particular, it provides not only the possibility to apply administrative sanctions for the breaching of Commission Decision 98/653/EC but also a clarification on the extension of the ban on the consignment to be sent to the Azores (see also XXIV/1044 and 1061/99, as regards the interpretation of the word "dispatch"). Certainly, according to the declaration of the Portuguese authorities, the lack of shipping lines between Azores and the other Member States results in the difficulty of exporting cattle to Azores (POSEIMA project). III.2 Implementation of the export ban III.2.1 The implementation of the road checks 11 DG(SANCO)/1227/1999/MR Final The mission team verified that, for the time being, there was no improvement regarding the system of road checks. In particular, the system is working on the same basis already verified in the mission carried out in June 1999 (XXIV/1061/99), without any correction as suggested in the recommendations to that report. Taking into account the declaration of the PA, this area needs to be further assessed in a future mission. III.2.2 Controls at the point of exit An improvement is recognised in this area: the direct access to the information on the consignments to be sent to Third Countries now allows the BIP staff to carry out proper control, without taking into consideration the exporter's declaration. This improvement addresses satisfactorily the specific recommendations already provided in previous mission (in particular, XXIV/1044 and 1061/99), even though more specific instructions could avoid different approaches by the different BIPs. Certainly, this improvement regards only a part of the "commercial traffic" of Portugal: the difficulty to build up a control system on the number of consignments to be sent to the Member States (according to the declaration of the PA) can result in the tendency to rely too much on the Shipping agencies. The fact, that the Veterinary Services can not inspect consignments without the presence of both the Custom Services and the exporter, undermines the overall efficiency of the controls. Although the Veterinary Services are designated as the competent authority as regards the controls on export ban, they do not have all the power necessary to carry out the controls effectively. III.2.3 The "Triangular trade" (Chapter IV Commission Decision 98/653/EC ) The global revision of this area could be considered complete by the adoption of the Manual of Operation for the plant interested in being approved in the framework of Art.9 of Commission Decision 98/653/EC, if the Manual is a compulsory step for the plant and not a rule to be adopted on a voluntary basis. III.3 Animal Identification system III.3.1 The controls in place and the application of the Council Regulation 2630/97 · The on farm controls only began in the middle of September 1999, after the training courses that the Central Authority provided to the specifically recruited staff (34 units for 17 teams). As regards the total number of controls that the PA should have already carried out (as foreseen in the CR) for the time being they are few (only 3 farms in the Region of Beira Litoral) , and this will result in a delay on the application of the CR 2630/97, applicable since 1.1.1998 (for 1998, no on farm controls were declared to have been carried out) · The organisation of the controls is not yet completely satisfactory: the list of the specific farms to be controlled was not yet built up and the Portuguese Authorities were not fully aware of the sampling criteria in Article 2 of Commission Regulation 2630/97/EC (risk analysis). 12 DG(SANCO)/1227/1999/MR Final · The instructions provided to the animal identification inspectors and, more generally, on the animal identification system, do not foresee the registration of origin and the date of entry of the cattle when a new Herd Register is built up, with the consequence that it is difficult (sometimes impossible) to recover all the information on the cattle born or introduced in the farm before the new register. · The use of the new form of declaration of cattle movement is not completely clear; · The mission team noted discrepancy between the number and the identification of the cattle in the farm and the cattle registered in the SNIRB system. · The instructions to the animal identification inspectors do not indicate a need to specify deadlines for the farmer to comply with the EU rules, nor how to apply specific administrative sanctions or restrictions to the movement of the cattle. III.3.2. The SNIRB System · The validation of input data is only partially applied at the moment. Moreover, data available from other sources (i.e. inspections, PISA and SINGA) are not used to their full extent for such validation. Both the 'simple' validation procedures and logical validation are of the utmost importance as decreased quality of the data reduces the value of the whole system. · As the results of on-farm controls are not recorded in the current or any other database, it is impossible to verify from the database if any restrictions have been applied to a given animal or herd. The effectiveness of sampling for on-farm inspections, follow-up of non-compliance and checking for eligibility of an animal would be significantly enhanced if the status of each animal was recorded in the database. · Although the database provides the basic data needed for tracing back and forward, full support for tracing activities is not yet included in the system. This might not be of a serious concern at the moment as tracing of BSE birth cohorts for example, depends on data in other systems. In order to be regarded as fully operational, the system should provide all the services expected from it. · Currently the system does not provide support for a selective export scheme. · The intention of the Portuguese Authorities is to integrate SNIRB with PISA (bovine health database) and SINGA (premium database). However, at the time of the mission it was not quite clear how this is to be achieved. The process of integration can be evaluated only after clear objectives and details of the practical implementation are available. III.4 The BSE surveillance and eradication III.4.1 Even though the mission team recognises that the Portuguese authorities are making every effort to trace the animals involved in a BSE case, the tracing operation can not 13 DG(SANCO)/1227/1999/MR Final be considered closed until all the information, also that coming from further and new sources, can be evaluated. III.4.2 The procedure for histological examination that LNIV is following is the one laid down in the OIE standards (Chapter 3.2.13). Even though one more location is added to the ones foreseen in the OIE standard, it was not completely clear if the midbrain examination can be considered as one of the 6 samples to control, or not. No explanation could be given for the high percentage of Listeria both in negative and in positive BSE cases. III.4.3 · The recommendations in mission re

recommendations.text: An urgent and sustained effort should be made to improve co- operation between the various ministries, laboratories and other government agencies involved in controls over milk production at central, regional and local levels. Procedures for monitoring the performance of regional and local services should be established, so that a clear picture of compliance with the relevant Community legislation can be obtained by the central authorities9.

All relevant provisions of Community legislation, and in particular: 8 In their response to the draft report, the Portuguese Authorities noted that this conclusion was based on results from one source only. They considered the percentage of truck silos that tested positive for inhibitory substances to be low. 9 See footnote 1. 20 (a) Article 10 (on-farm treatment registers), Council Directive 96/23/EC10 (b) Article 14 (HACCP principles), Council Directive 92/46/EEC (c) Annex A, Chapter I (presence of violative residues), Council Directive 92/46/EEC (d) Annex A, Chapter IV (raw milk quality), Council Directive 92/46/EEC (e) Article 3 (accreditation of laboratories), Council Directive 93/99/EEC, should be immediately transposed (where necessary) into Portuguese legislation and fully implemented and enforced.
In particular, immediate action should be taken to enforce proper controls over the presence of antibacterial residues in raw milk.
A sufficient number of suitably qualified staff, who have been adequately trained, should be available at all levels to ensure that milk production and processing is properly controlled11.
Sampling programmes for end products should be further developed so that all the requirements of Community legislation are met12.
Procedures for the approval of milk collection and processing establishments should be reviewed and improved in the light of the findings of this, and previous, FVO missions.

All dairy farms, milk collection centres and processing establishments should be reviewed in the light of this report, and action taken to ensure compliance with Community legislative standards. The Portuguese authorities should submit an action plan, indicating the action already taken or planned, and including a timetable, to address the conclusions a s of this report, within one month of receipt of the final report. 9.2. To the Commission Services (1) Consideration should be given to starting infringement proceedings against the Portuguese authorities, in light of their failure to transpose, implement and enforce elements of Community legislation, as indicated above. 10 See footnote 5. 11 See footnote 4. 12 See footnote 3. 21 (2) The action plan requested from the Portuguese authorities should be carefully reviewed to evaluate whether it responds satisfactorily to the report's conclusions a s. ADDENDUM In its fax and letter dated 15 March 2002 and 19 March 2002, respectively, the Portuguese Authorities made comments which have, where possible, been included in the text of the report. Actions have been taken to improve the co- operation between the different departments responsible for controls over milk production (recommendation 9.1.1). Publishing of the order (Portaria) laying down the model for a register of treatments with veterinary drugs, which is to be kept by owners of cattle-holdings or animals producing food for human consumption, is in progress (recommendation 9.1.2.(a). The Portuguese competent authorities are continuing to organise further training for the inspectors responsible for milk hygiene control (recommendation 9.1.4) and are developing further their sampling programmes (recommendation 9.1.5). 22

audits.title: Production et mise sur le marché de viande fraîche porcine, de gibier et de lapin

recommendations.text: The approval of the rabbit slaughterhouse/cutting-plant has been suspended until the structural, operational and hygiene deficiencies have been resolved.

The veterinary officer assigned to the pig slaughterhouse/cutting-plant has been replaced by a new colleague who will be trained by the DGV. The structural and operational deficiencies were the subject of a remedial action plan to be assessed by the Portuguese authorities during October 2001. II. On 14 December 2001, the Portuguese authorities faxed a document setting out the principles of the action taken or to be taken in follow-up to the report's conclusions. 4

Portaria n° 518/2001, the base for the implementation of Commission Decision 2001/218/EC in Portugal, has to be adjusted on the following points: - the obligation to cut all coniferous trees showing symptoms of poor health or situated in salvage areas in the buffer zone has to be included; 20 - the delimitation of the demarcated area has to be adapted: the affected zone must include all coniferous stands that are known to be affected with PWN (e.g. the public estate Companhia das Lezirias) and the whole buffer zone has to be at least 20 Km wide, including in the region around Lisbon and the estuary of the river Tejo.

The eradication campaign for the coming winter must be completed for the entire demarcated area before 1 April 2002. The eradication must include all symptomatic coniferous trees in the buffer zone, whether infested with PWN or not.
Detailed, written instructions should be given to the monitoring teams about the transport conditions of wood samples.
Efforts have to be made to collect more scientific evidence about the lifecycle of Monochamus galloprovincialis under climatic conditions, similar to these in Portugal.
All logs that are stored in the demarcated area during the period from 2 April to 31 October, have to be debarked.
The correct application of quarantine treatments (fumigation, heat treatment, insecticide treatment, burning) has to be checked systematically by the local inspectors. Records must be kept.

No exceptions should be made to the use of the appropriate transport document when moving non treated construction timber from non-symptomatic trees locally within the demarcated area. The Competent Authorities of Portugal are requested to submit to the Commission, within two months of receipt of the final report, an action plan addressing the above recommendations and giving deadlines for their implementation. 9.2. To the Commission Services 1) The creation of specific exemptions for wood, originating in pest free zones and moved to the demarcated area could be considered when reviewing the Commission Decision 2001/218/EC. 2) Corrective actions by the CA as mentioned under 9.1 should be followed up closely. 10. ADDENDUM In their comments to the draft report, the Portuguese authorities have generally accepted the recommendations and will cover them by legal requirements or improvements to the existing system. In relation to 9.1. 1), second indent, Portugal confirmed to include immediately in the affected zone that part of the public estate that tested positive for the presence of PWN in 2001. 21

audits.title: Plant health system in the potato sector

recommendations.text: As far as the outbreak of Ralstonia solanacearum is concerned Portugal states that "Given the characteristics of the farms and production systems in the areas where outbreaks of infection with the bacteria were detected, it was not always possible, despite the great efforts made, to precisely identify the origin of the contamination and, therefore, to successfully carry out all the surveys that were needed. Whenever infected potato fields were found, the quarantine measures required under the Directive were taken. In the case of fields that were probably contaminated, it was decided to subject them to more intensive official checks, stepping up inspection of the crops growing there. As regards contaminated irrigation water, the fact that laboratory tests on samples collected from the same watercourse at different dates often produced both positive and negative results made it difficult to have a clear overview of the situation and to take the radical step of banning irrigation. However, the Authorities kept the situation under control, issuing circulars drawing attention to the risk to plants and recommending that the water not be used to irrigate solanacea crops".
Portugal will devise a contingency plan by the end of this year to deal with any future outbreak of Clavibacter michiganensis ssp. sepedonicus. A copy of the plan will then be sent to the Commission.

Taking account of existing laboratory capacity, Portugal will make an attempt this year to adapt the control plan by increasing the number of tests carried out on Portuguese ware potatoes in order to detect Ralstonia solanacearum.
An attempt will be made to increase the official supervision of the PCN tests processed by the accredited body. 25

audits.title: Fishery products and live bivalve molluscs

recommendations.text: As response (dated 12/03/2002) to the request from the FVO (dated 7 February 2002): - Three establishments visited by the mission team were inspected by the Portuguese services. As a result the approval one establishment was suspended and another was given deadlines for the implementation of corrective actions. - The competent authority started before the FVO mission a complete round of inspections in all approved establishments in order to evaluate compliance with directive 91/493/EEC. So far, these are the results of these inspections: * 3 Establishments whose approval was cancelled and the control number was withdrawn; * 3 Establishments whose approval is in process of cancelling. * 11 Establishments whose approval was cancelled and the control number is in process of withdrawn; * 5 Establishments whose approval and control number is in phase of cancelling; * 1 Establishment in phase of licence reformulating; * 3 Establishments in full compliance with the 91/493/EEC directive. - Additional information was provided on the production and trade of oysters originating from the area Lagos Zona litoral. - An updated list was sent of 25 auctions, 9 warehouses, 1 wholesale market, 4 factory vessels and 8 fish processing establishments which are established/based at the Azores.

With their comments on the draft mission report (dated 17 June 2002): - DGV and DGPA started joint technical visits to fishing vessels staying at sea for more than 24 hours with the aim all such fishing vessels. Visits to 30 vessels in the Algarve region are already scheduled; - Changes in the legislation are foreseen to clarify the competencies between the different authorities involved in the official control; - Technical visits to nine establishments were carried and it is planned to visit the remaining establishments before the end the current year; - The planned establishment of a Sanitary Fish Inspection Service is being effectuated at present, in particular to check the follow up of the technical visits; 27 - The plan for chemical control of fresh fish sold at auctions was approved and is due to be implemented soon; - A quality system will be put in place and written procedures for the IPIMAR Laboratory in Olhão will be drafted by the end of 2002; - Written procedures for sampling and transport of samples for the IPIMAR Laboratory in Lisbon are being drafted; - The results of positive laboratory analyses, carried out by IPIMAR, will be transmitted in writing; - Training is planned for private persons, external to IPIMAR, carrying out the sampling. Its implementation is foreseen to be finished by the end of 2002; - The establishment of boundaries and of fixed sampling points in the production areas for bivalve molluscs will be finalised in the first semester of 2003; - Written procedures for several steps in the sampling are being drafted. Its finalisation is foreseen in the third trimester of 2002; - The sampling programme for biotoxins and phytoplancton is being reviewed; - IPIMAR Lisbon is already implementing the method for E.coli recommended by the CRL (CEFAS in Weymouth). The request to the national accreditation body (IPQ) for the accreditation of the method is foreseen in 2003; - IPIMAR Lisbon is putting in place a quality system to be finalised by the end of 2002. It is not covering all the relevant requirements of the ISO Norm 17025, in particular those related to staff and premises; - IPIMAR Lisbon will carry out supervision audits of the IPIMAR regional laboratories performing microbiological analyses in the second semester 2002.

audits.title: Traçabilité des viandes fraîches et des produits bovins depuis l'élevage jusqu'à la mise sur le marché

recommendations.text: Inform the Commission of the measures taken in the farms and cutting plants visited by the inspection team to correct the major deficiencies found. These measures should be notified to the Commission within a month of receiving the draft report.

Adjust the way in which official controls are carried out in bovine holdings; in particular, allocate sufficient manpower for this purpose, taking account of all the risk factors contained in Article 2 of Regulation EC) No 2630/97.
As a short-term measure, update the data base covering bovine animals, their identification and movement, in order to eliminate the deficiencies found during the mission. 2

Step up official controls in cutting plants/minced-meat plants, especially to focus more effectively on verifying the traceability of bovine meat and products. The measures referred to in points 8.1.2, 8.1.3 and 8.1.4 should be the subject of an action plan, accompanied by a schedule, which should be submitted to the Commission within three months following receipt of the final report. 8.2. To the Commission services 8.2.1. Evaluate the measures and action plan submitted by the competent Portuguese authorities. 8.2.2. Take appropriate steps if the competent authorities fail to follow up the recommendations contained in this report. ADDENDUM In a letter dated 30 April 2002, the Portuguese authorities gave their comments on the content of the draft report. In the same correspondence, they informed the FVO of the measures already taken or envisaged in response to the report's recommendations. 3
To ensure that the bovine brucellosis programme is given the necessary attention and resources to allow further progress. Herds should be classified according to the EU legislative requirements.
To reinforce animal movement controls, so as to prevent the movement of sheep from infected flocks, other than direct to slaughter.
To ensure that the birth of calves is notified within the period foreseen in Regulation No. 1760/2000.
To reinforce and enhance the control and supervision of the activities of the OPPs.
To ensure that all reactor cattle are removed from farms within 45 days of official notification of the owner, as specified in the approved eradication programme.

To ensure that suspended (non-certified) laboratories are required to make the necessary improvements. The OPPs/DRAs should encourage the submission of samples from aborted animals to laboratories for analysis.
To address the other deficiencies in the implementation of the BBEP noted in this report.

To take the necessary action to address the identified shortcomings in food safety controls. An action plan for the implementation of the above recommendations and conclusions, including deadlines for action, should be sent to the Commission Services within two months of receipt of the final translated report. 9.2. To the Commission Services 9.2.1 To review future eradication programmes in the light of the findings, conclusions and recommendations of this report. ADDENDUM Competent authority's response to the draft report In a letter dated 9 January 2003 responding to the draft report, the Competent Authority described action taken in response to the recommendations: 9.1.1 Instructions were given to the Regional Veterinary Services to perform a proper classification of herds with B4 status and those with B3 status which have not been vaccinated in the last 3 years. A request is to be 18 made in January 2003 to the Regional Veterinary Services to indicate a veterinarian responsible for the eradication programme. This veterinarian will be monitoring the measures taken in the region, as well as evaluating with the OPP(s) and DGV the progress and targets achieved every 3 months. Instructions, with the procedures to be followed, have already been given to the Regional Veterinary Services to evaluate the serological controls performed and the evolution of the health status of herds from the PISA database. 9.1.2 Instructions were given in December 2002 to the Regional Veterinary Services to reinforce the controls over the movement of sheep/goats from infected flocks through a programme of inspections to be made on-the- spot. 9.1.3 Attention will be given from now on to ensure that the birth of calves will be notified within the period foreseen in Regulation No 1760/2000. 9.1.4 The DGV is already performing the control and supervision of the activities of OPP(s) through field audits and these activities are to be maintained. 9.1.5 Instructions will be given this month to the Regional Veterinary Services to assure the removal of animals from farms within 45 days of official notification. 9.1.6 As from 1 January 2003, laboratories not complying with rules defined by the National Reference Laboratory and related to the quality of results, will not receive more blood samples until the situation is addressed. 9.1.7 It is the understanding of the Portuguese CA that all deficiencies described in the conclusions of the report are included in the recommendations and hence, no more deficiencies need to be addressed. 9.1.8 The shortcomings identified in the food safety controls on the health mark (observed in the slaughterhouse) will be addressed during January 2003. The procedure followed in the slaughterhouse was not in accordance with rules established at national level, which require that meat from sanitary slaughter cannot be traded within the Community nor exported to third countries. Following approval, only the national health mark may be applied (Annex provided by the CA referring to the relevant circular and regulations). The information on milk from infected herds was addressed again in November 2002 to the Regional Veterinary Services. The Portuguese CA added that during December 2002, a two day meeting took place at the DGV with all Regional Veterinary Services in order to evaluate the eradication programmes (measures in place, targets to achieve, measures to be changed or reinforced and the recommendations in this report).

The deficiencies related to the procedures should be corrected immediately and in particular: The delivery of non-EC-conforming consignments to caterers by authorised ship suppliers, as already mentioned in report DG/SANCO/1266/2000.

Action should be taken to correct all other deficiencies noted in this report [general findings (as legislation, supervision etc), training, facilities ­ except the major deficiencies referred to in point 8.1.3, equipment, hygiene, documentation, registration, identification and selection, procedure, kitchen waste, free and customs warehouses and ship suppliers]. In any event all deficiencies should be corrected within three months of receipt of the final translated report, according to Article 6 of Commission Decision 2001/812/EC and in particular: Facilities: The minor deficiencies described under point 5.2.7. Identification: All the deficiencies described under point 5.2.13. Procedures: All the deficiencies described under point 5.2.14 should be corrected satisfactorily. Portugal should ensure that veterinary checks on consignments of products are carried out in accordance with the requirements laid down in Council Directive 97/78/EC and related Commission Decisions.

The major deficiencies of the facilities (construction other than those mentioned in 8.1.2) referred to in this report should be corrected 21 within six months of receipt of the final report, according to Article 6 of Commission Decision 2001/812/EC and in particular for: Peniche, Aveiro, Viana do Castelo, Portimao and Olhao. 8.2. To the Commission It is recommended that the Commission: 8.2.1. Consider withdrawal of the approval of the border inspection posts mentioned under 8.1.1, 8.1.2 and 8.1.3 if satisfactory guarantees in relation to the approval (type of category) are not provided within the relevant time limit by the Portuguese authorities. 8.2.2. Consider limiting the approval of the BIPs of Peniche, Portimao and Olhao to packed products (footnote 2) if satisfactory guarantees in relation to the approval (type of category) are not provided within the relevant time limit by the Portuguese authorities. 22 9. ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT DG(SANCO)/8559/2002 Competent Central Authority response to the recommendations in the report 9.1. Response to recommendations CCA provided in its comments guarantees to some shortcomings noted in the report. 9.2. Response to recommendations 8.1.1. CCA has sent a fax to all the authorities responsible for the facilities to ensure compliance with the legislation prohibiting the supply of non- conforming products to caterers. Furthermore, the establishments in question will submit to DGV-DSCV a monthly report on incoming and outgoing goods. 9.3. Response to recommendations 8.1.2.

Cooperation A new system has been implemented for the receipt of notifications under the Rapid Alert System, in which notifications are sent via email directly by the Direcção Geral de Fiscalização e Controlo da Qualidade Alimentar (Directorate-General for Food Quality Inspection and Control) to DGV (DSCV) as soon as it receives them. CCA has sent a fax to the Regional Directorates of Agriculture to draw their attention once again to the need to send to the BIPs the lists of establishments or other documentation in good time. Now that Portimão and Olhão have fax machines, CCA can send them information directly. 5.2.13. Identification and selection of consignments CCA sent a copy to the Direcção Geral das Alfândegas e dos Impostos Especials sobre o Consumo (directorate-general for customs and special taxes on consumption) of the positive list clearly indicating the previously omitted items. Before the Commission visit, a contact list had been prepared with all details entered in advance at local level, indicating the names of the persons responsible in the various bodies (customs, port administrations and others) and the places where manifests and ship lists could be consulted. 5.2.2. Legislation CCA has requested a meeting with the Instituto da Conservação da Natureza (nature conservation institute) with a view to asking again for correction of notice No 1999/C, 356/028. A meeting was held with the Laboratório Nacional de Investigação Veterinária (national veterinary research laboratory) in order to start drawing up a national plan for laboratory analysis at BIP level. A second meeting was subsequently held to secure the involvement of the Instituto de Investigação das Pescas e do Mar (institute for fisheries and marine research) and the 23 Directorate-General for Fisheries in this plan. Following these meetings, rules have now been drawn up for fisheries products. 5.2.3. Supervision CCA have sent the records of findings to the various BIPs, along with the draft report as well. A checklist has been prepared for procedures for the identification and selection of consignments for documentary, identity and physical checks. The BIPs in Setúbal and Lisbon have been visited to inspect these procedures to follow up mission report DG(SANCO)/1261/2000. DGV is drawing up the record of findings to be sent to the various BIPs regarding procedures. Along with the sending of the Commission report to all the BIPs, CCA believes that the programme of visits launched by DGV, together with the forwarding of the findings of these visits to the BIPs, and the training courses launched can progressively eliminate a number of deficiencies. 5.2.6. Tranining DGV is continuing to provide training courses. Such courses have been held for both veterinary technicians and administrative technicians of the BIPs in Olhão, Portimão and Lisbon (two persons in the latter case) to provide further training in the operation of and data entry for the database for the registration of goods and in the ANIMO system. 5.2.7. Facilities As the lift in Peniche was not for the exclusive use of the BIP, it was decided to close it permanently. 5.2.8. Facilities outside the BIP but used for the BIP Where rejected consignments are concerned, they must now always be sent to establishments approved under the provisions of Directive 90/667/EEC or, alternatively, to locations/establishments for incineration 5.2.9. Equipment DGV has been procuring various equipment for all the BIPs, assuming responsibility for all these procurements. 5.2.11 Documentation All the BIPs have been sent a copy of Joint Committee Decision EEA No. 69/98 (list of BIPs approved in Norway and Iceland). 5.2.14. Prodedures A circular has been prepared setting out the items that must be contained in captain declaration (Council Regulation 1093/94/EC). 24 9.4. Response to recommendation 8.1.3. Facilities At central level, all the port administrations were sent the mission report and a fax requesting details of their intentions regarding the need to restructure their facilities, to which only one response has been received, from the administration of the Port of Aveiro, and indicating in summary form the requirements for the planning of these facilities under Commission Decision 2002/812/EC, in particular Article 6.

audits.title: Implementation of Commission Decision 2001-218-EC and its amendment and assessment of the eradication programme for Bursaphelenchus Xylophilus

recommendations.text: To the competent authorities of Portugal · The CA should send an action plan to the Commission services as requested in mission report 3404/2001. 12 · The Portuguese national legislation must stipulate a clear and identical interpretation of the term "[susceptible plants] showing any symptoms of poor health" mentioned in Commission Decision 2001/218/EC. · The surveyors' manual should be updated to include detailed information of all symptoms of trees that have to be cut. · The cutting of remaining trees in poor health in the demarcated area should be finalised as soon as possible. · Private gardens should be included in the campaign. · The monitoring of the Lisbon area should be done at the same time as the buffer zone. · The CA should ensure that records of every inspection carried out are kept. · Publicity on the actions and results of the yearly campaign should increase. · A long-term plan with a more active strategy on the eradication of PWN from the Portuguese territory should be developed and implemented. The Competent Authority of Portugal is requested to submit to the Commission, within two months of receipt of the final report, an action plan addressing the above recommendations and giving deadlines for their implementation.

To the Commission Services The long-term planning and implementation of the strategy as mentioned under 9.1 has to be followed up. 10. ADDENDUM In their comments to the draft report, the CA stipulated that the Portuguese national legislation uses the term `conifers that show symptoms of infestation with PWN' for describing the trees with any symptoms of poor health as referred to in Commission Decision 2001/218/EC. An extra conclusion and recommendation is added in this final report to guarantee that the possible confusion on this point is clarified. 13

The competent authorities (CAs) should rectify the shortcomings found in the various establishments visited during this mission and mentioned in this report. In relation to the different areas covered in this mission, the following more detailed recommendations are made: 8.1.1.1.CA performance i. The CCAs should improve the co-operation between themselves and between the different services at regional level and, consequently, ii. improve the level of information with a view to defining and managing the priorities regarding eggs and egg products, iii. a decision should be taken upon which one of the CCAs is responsible for the breaking section of the egg packing centres, iv. the CCAs should establish effective collaboration and co-operation with the CAs of the Autonomous Regions of Azores and Madeira in the operation of egg packing centre/egg product establishment approval, v. the list of approved packing centres and egg product establishments should be updated. 8.1.1.2.Approval procedures for egg packing centres / egg processing establishments i. The re-approval system for approved establishments intending to modify or change their establishment or field of operations should be followed, ii. the approval of egg packing centres with an egg breaking section should be explicitly addressed, in accordance with the Directive. 7 8.1.1.3.Official supervision of egg packing centres, egg products establishments or establishments using eggs or egg products as raw material i. Effectiveness of the overall official supervision of establishments producing and/or processing egg products needs to be improved. 8.1.1.4.Own checks i. The CAs should ensure that testing for verification of analytical specifications of egg products is carried out in compliance with the requirements of Chapter VI of the Directive's Annex. 8.1.1.5.Chilling of raw material and/or products i. The CAs should ensure that the Directive's requirements with regard to chilling of non-pasteurised egg products are always complied with. 8.1.1.6.Trade in eggs and egg products ­ Traceability ­ Export and certification i. The CAs should take the necessary measures to ensure that labelling of non-pasteurised egg product is properly done.
The CAs should also take appropriate action to rectify such shortcomings in all other approved establishments in Portugal.

The CAs should inform the Commission services of the progress and results of the measures taken, within two months following receipt of the final report, including a timetable for completion by a reasonable deadline of measures and actions still outstanding. 8.2. To the Commission Services None. 8 9. ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT DG (SANCO)/8606/2002 Central Competent Authorities' response to the recommendations in the report The CCAs of Portugal have informed the FVO in their communications of 21 June 2002 and 17 July 2002 that they accepted most of the recommendations of the draft report. These communications also provided the following information about the actions and measures taken or planned to be taken in response to the main findings and recommendations in the report: · With regard to the third paragraph of 4.5.2.: the DGV stated that it is going to carry out a re-assessment of the current situation in order to correct it. · With regard to 8.1.1.1.: the DGFCQA informed about measures taken to improve co- ordination with the DGV. 9
To take appropriate measures aimed at ensuring the systematic sampling of fallen stock over 24 months.

To take appropriate measures to ensure the correct classification of the animals in the BSE testing programme in the respective sub-population. In particular it should be ensured that animals from the eradication campaigns are properly classified.
To establish an efficient system for monitoring the BSE testing programme at various levels, which allows a system for prompt corrective actions where needed.
To establish a system where the compliance of the NRL with EU requirements is ensured.

To clarify the status of the LNIV in Oporto and to ensure that it meets the requirements attached to that status (as a regional laboratory if needed). In addition, the verification of its performance, in relation to HP and IHC should be urgently addressed. With regard to TSE monitoring in small ruminants 1. To take measures to ensure the correct application of the sheep and goats' identification and registration system and to include all holdings of sheep and goats in the PISA as soon as possible. The traceability of progeny and cohorts of eventual TSEs cases should be considered in the context of the new legislation in preparation. 2. To take measures to increase the level of awareness of Scrapie among the farming community. 22 3. To take measures to ensure that the monitoring programme is carried out up to the level set up in Regulation (EC) 999/2001, Annex III, A.II.2 and A.II.3. 4. To draw up a contingency plan for TSEs in small ruminants as soon as possible. With regard to the feed ban 1. To take measures to ensure a prompt implementation of Decision 2001/9/EC, and to verify its practical implementation in the regions. 2. To take measures to ensure that the plants are consistently authorised in accordance with Decision 2001/9/EC, based on evidence that its requirements are fulfilled. 3. To take measures to ensure that the sampling programme meets the targeting criteria established in Directive 95/53/EC. 4. To review the current organisation of the feed controls, in order to ensure a better co-ordination and exchange of information between the bodies involved in the implementation of the programme, and to provide for a comprehensive control system. 5. To take measures to ensure that the sampling method laid down in Directive 76/371/EC is applied regardless of the premises where the sampling is performed.
To ensure that the channelling procedure and the sampling of the imported derogated PAP is fully applied
To take measures to verify the performance of the feed laboratory in order to ensure that the requirement laid down in art. 18 (2) of Directive 95/53/EC are fully met.

To take measures to ensure that the results from the microscopic analysis test can be provided within a time framework that would allow prompt corrective action. With regard to SRM 1. To strengthen controls aimed at ensuring the channelling of SRM throughout the chain. 2. To take measures aimed at ensuring that only rendering plants which comply with the requirements set out in Decision 1999/534/EC, are authorised. A system for corrective actions where deficiencies were found should be established. 3. To ensure that SRM which has not been sterilised in accordance with the requirements set out in Decision 1999/534/EC, is not landfilled. 23 ADDENDUM Response of the competent authorities to the recommendations An action plan from the Portuguese CCA to address the recommendations in the draft report for which urgent action was sought was received on 11 February 2003. The relevant part of this may be summarised as follows: With regard to BSE epidemio-surveillance: · A system for the collection and sampling of fallen stock over 12 month of age is in operation since 1 February 2003, and it will be refined and extended from 1 April 2003. The system will be monitored by the INGA, DGV and LNIV. · Guidelines on the rules for the systematic categorisation of animals in the sub- populations referred to in Regulation (EC) No 999/2001 have been issued by means of Circular letter No 298 of 15.12.2002, addressed to the DRAs, OPPs and inspectors at slaughterhouses. Forms used to accompany the samples taken at slaughterhouse level have been modified to avoid confusions, in particular as regards animals slaughtered in the framework of sanitation campaigns. Training on the proper implementation of categorisation for inspectors at slaughterhouses and OPPs' practitioners has been already organised or is under way. · A National co-ordinator for BSE and BSE related issues will be appointed immediately. The co-ordinator, who will report directly to the Director General for Veterinary Services, will be responsible for guaranteeing the uniform and proper implementation of the relevant rules in the BSE field. With regard to the feed ban: · The legal instrument implementing Decision 2001/9/EC is scheduled to be approved in February 2003. · The authorisation for establishments using PAP was considered no longer valid after January 2003. New documentation, including the diagram of the separated production lines and an own-control programme, had to be submitted for re- approval. An authorisation could be granted after an on-the-spot inspection to the premises. · It is foreseen to reduce the time needed to provide the results from the microscopic analysis test acting on: ­ Collection of samples, which will be better distributed during time and targeted to detect the possible use of PAP (according to the Programme of official inspections on feedingstuffs for 2003). ­ Processing of results documentation, which will be faster. ­ Testing resources, for which the LNIV in Oporto will be authorised to perform the analysis on the presence of PAP. With regard to SRM: · Measurement devices in the rendering plant where shortcomings were detected have been subjected to calibration. This ensures that SRM is properly sterilised. ____________________ 24

audits.title: PAH (Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons) contamination of vegetable oils

recommendations.text: Take urgent steps to develop official control laboratory capability for analysis of the 8 PAH established in Portuguese legislation. Base the official control of refined lots on analysis for the 8 PAH.
Take measures to enhance the official control activities for PAH, particularly of new production and take measures to improve the implementation and enforcement of systems based on HACCP principles.

Extracting plants should be regarded as food business and thus food regulations should be applied to them, to correctly apply the provisions of relevant Community legislation, in particular Regulation (EC) 178/2002 of the European Parliament and of the Council and Council Directive 89/397/ECC. 24

Adequate and complete information on the food companies operating in the regions should be available for inspection purposes. A programme in response to these recommendations should be produced by the competent authority, which should provide detailed information of the actions that will be taken and propose deadlines by which these actions will be completed within 2 months of receipt of the final report. 11. ADDENDUM The DGFCQA in their response stated that they had notified to the first company that it had to implement safety procedures based on HACCP within a period of 180 days. That period expired at the end of 2002. Inspectors will go and check that the procedures have been implemented. The competent authority also stressed that production and consumption of olive pomace oil are not very high in Portugal, and that there has been a decrease in processing and marketing since July 2001. 25

audits.title: Animal welfare during transport and at the time of slaughter

recommendations.text: Transporters and slaughtermen receive the training required by Article 5 of Council Directive 91/628/EEC (as amended) and Article 7 of Council Directive 93/119/EEC.
More harmonised checks are carried out, which cover the specific criteria set in EU Directives, particularly in slaughterhouses.
The target set for checks is achieved, and that in every case when a deficiency is detected, corrective and follow up action is taken, and where necessary a sanction is applied.

Animals transported by sea receive the care foreseen in Chapter I.D of the Annex of Council Directive 91/628/EEC (as amended), particularly concerning enough and adequate provision of water and foodstuff, and protection against weather, and that all animals are transported in clean and adequately bedded containers.

VIs in the slaughterhouses are aware that it is the transporter's duty to return the route plan to the place of origin, as required by Article 5.A.d of Council Directive 91/628/EEC (as amended), in the context of future training.

Only animals fit for the intended journey are transported, as required by Article 3.1.b of Council Directive 91/628/EEC (as amended) and Article 12 of Council Directive 93/119/EC. audits.title: Control of Residues in live animals and animal products

recommendations.text: To ensure that the number of staff deployed in the context of supervising the NRCP, implementing controls on Direct Acquisition Outlets, manufacturers of medicated premixes and producers of medicated feedingstuffs, are commensurate with the diverse nature and volume of these activities.
To ensure that all relevant Community legislation is transposed in the area of VMPs and residues control.

To formally agree and adequately monitor adherence to performance indicators for all parties involved in the administration of residues controls (e.g. turnaround times for the laboratory and sampling schedules for DRA) in order to ensure sampling, reporting and follow up activities are carried out as rapidly as is practicable.
To consider clarifying the current criteria for conduction of follow up sampling in response to MRL violations in order to enhance the effectiveness of control measures.
To ensure that marketing authorisations and label indications for VMPs are reviewed in light of the findings of this report.

To improve overall co-ordination with INFARMED in the application of controls on VMPs, ensuring that distribution of such substances is adequately monitored and that the supply of authorised VMPs to species for which they are not intended, is effectively prohibited.
To ensure that the staffing quotient in the laboratory network is adequate for effective residues monitoring in a quality controlled environment (i.e. accredited facility).

To ensure that all analytical methods for residues are fit for purpose and adequately validated. _________________ 15 ADDENDUM TO MISSION REPORT 9209/2003 Response of the Portuguese competent authorities to the recommendations in the draft report received by letter dated 26 February 2004. In advance of an Action Plan requested from the CCA following production of the final report, both Portuguese central competent authorities (DGV and INFARMED) have already made a number of commitments and proposals to address some of the deficiencies outlined in the draft report. These can be summarised as follows (grouped by recommendation number, if applicable). Recommendation 2. INFARMED has undertaken to immediately transpose the amended version of the codified Directive 2001/82/EC into national legislation, after publication in the Official Journal of the Communities. This will be achieved by synchronising actions with a view to improving general co-ordination between both DGV and INFARMED. The plan will be launched in 2004 and quarterly meetings will be held between both CCAs. The plan will consist of five components ­ (1) Control and surveillance [of raw materials and VMPs ­ a schedule for the number of inspections at each of the main `sites' and the composition of the inspection teams has been included], (2) Review of old VMPs [marketing authorisations granted before 1987], (3) Legislative action [draft Decree Laws have been prepared pertaining to medicated feedingstuffs and use of VMPs on pig farms], (4) Good Manufacturing Practice guidelines [for pre- mix and medicated feedingstuffs manufacture], (5) Dissemination of standards and legislation [in order to prevent improper use of VMPs]. Furthermore with regard to Recommendation 7, INFARMED has stated that during 2004 a system for the codification of pharmacological VMPs for the automatic acquisition of data (marketing authorisation ­ batch ­ shelf life ­ quantity) will be implemented. 16

To strengthen the supervision of controls aimed at ensuring full and uniform application of legal provisions and instructions on proper channelling of SRM from 12 all establishments where they are removed up to the final destruction of the material. _______________________ 13 ADDENDUM Response of the competent authorities to the recommendations Comments from the Portuguese CCA on the draft report were received on 23 April 2004, and included an outline of some actions planned and/or undertaken to address certai s contained in the report. These may be summarised as follows: With regard to BSE epidemio-surveillance: 1. Progress has been made as regards setting of new criteria for the annual control plan of inspections being implemented during 2004. Further importance is given to those holdings where specific non-compliances with sanitary requirements were found as well as to those that have sent animals with identification problems to slaughterhouses. At the end of the first quarter more than a half of the inspections to be carried out during 2004 have been already decided and planned. 2. Current provisions for infringements of I&R non-compliances have been reviewed in order to ease up this process. In addition, a specific task force has been allocated to speed up all administrative procedures related with non-compliances in order to ensure timely corrective actions and sanctions where needed. 3. With regard to the feed ban: 1.
